subject: Status: Streaming chunk coalescing anomaly affecting EU customers (brief advisory)
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Eleanor Park <eleanor.park@lagombio.com>, sysops@lagombio.com
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 08 Sep 2027 15:47:00 +0000
Subject: Status: Streaming chunk coalescing anomaly affecting EU customers (brief advisory)

Hi Eleanor / Lagom sysops team,

Quick advisory from Redwood Inference — we detected an anomaly in the EU serving pool that intermittently delays the emission of streaming chunks for long-lived responses. Impact: about ~4% of streaming requests from the EU region experienced stretched chunk delivery or small partial payload drops between 14:30–15:20 UTC. You may see truncated/late incremental tokens in a subset of streamed responses; full-generation retries will still complete in most cases.

What we published: we posted an incident entry on our status page (link below) and routed your requests to an alternate pool while we investigate.

Mitigation in progress:
- We temporarily disabled the streaming coalescing optimization in the EU pool (this reduces per-token efficiency but prevents delayed chunk batching).
- Traffic routing: affected EU requests were shifted to the warm fallback pool with compatible latency SLAs.
- Short-term ask: if you have high-throughput streaming workloads that can tolerate slightly higher per-token cost, keep using the default endpoints; otherwise you can switch to the batch generation endpoint for non-interactive use.

Why this happened (initial): our telemetry shows a brief KV-cache eviction pattern combined with a coalescing timer misfire when load spiked on a small subset of hosts. The runtime team is triaging kernel scheduling and coalescing boundary conditions now.

Requested action from you: if you can, please share 1–3 request IDs or example timestamps (we've included a sampling code snippet on the status page) so we can correlate traces.

Attachments: statuspage-event-log.txt (short extract), screenshot-streaming-trace.png

We know this impacts user-facing experiences and apologize for the disruption. I will keep you updated as we have mitigations and a timeline for a permanent fix.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

--
For reference: https://status.redwood.inference/incidents/INC-20270908-eu-streaming
From: Eleanor Park <eleanor.park@lagombio.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 08 Sep 2027 16:02:31 +0000
Subject: Re: Status: Streaming chunk coalescing anomaly affecting EU customers (brief advisory)

Thanks Mina — appreciate the quick heads-up.

We saw the same thing in our monitoring (chat transcripts show missing incremental tokens intermittently). We've pulled three request ids from our logs around 14:42–14:46 UTC: req-ldg-00421, req-ldg-00435, req-ldg-00488. Sending them here and attaching a short sample of our client-side traces. Do you want these in a specific format?

Also — can you confirm whether the fallback pool has any differing model-version or quantization profile that might change output tokens? We're running a tight end-to-end comparison to ensure parity.

Eleanor Park
Platform Engineer, Lagom Bio
Eleanor.Park@lagombio.com

--
On Wed, Sep 8, 2027 at 15:47 Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Quick advisory from Redwood Inference — we detected an anomaly in the EU serving pool...

Attachments received: client-trace-sample.json
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Eleanor Park <eleanor.park@lagombio.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Sep 2027 18:10:05 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Status: Streaming chunk coalescing anomaly — action plan and CS notes

Team — forwarding Lagom's acknowledgment and sample request ids. Quick runbook we're executing: 
1) Correlate req-ids (req-ldg-00421, 00435, 00488) to host traces — priority.
2) Reproduce locally with coalescing enabled on the same model/sequence distribution.
3) Validate that fallback pool model config (variant "redwood-gptx-003-q8") is token-for-token equivalent for the request shapes Lagom uses; if not, we should trigger explicit parity validation.
4) Prepare a short customer note confirming ETA for a permanent fix and a timeline for the postmortem.

Notes: initial telemetry points at a scheduling race when the KV cache experienced transient evictions during a small cascade of prefix-heavy requests. Disabling coalescing reduced occurrences to near-zero (confirmed at 17:40 UTC).

Eleanor — can you confirm whether you observed any content-level drift when served from the fallback at 17:00–17:30 UTC? If you share 1–2 example outputs we'll compare diffs and tokenization boundaries.

I'll draft the public follow-up for the status page and a post-incident timeline after we validate parity.

Mina

--- Original message attached ---
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Eleanor Park <eleanor.park@lagombio.com>, sysops@lagombio.com
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 09 Sep 2027 02:12:00 +0000
Subject: Update: Incident resolved; postmortem + next steps (INC-20270908)

Hi Eleanor / Lagom ops,

Final update: the immediate impact window has been closed. Timeline summary:
- 14:30–15:20 UTC (09/08): onset; streaming chunk coalescing timer misfire + KV-cache evictions observed.
- 15:47 UTC: customer advisory published and traffic routed to fallback pool.
- 17:40 UTC: temporary mitigation (coalescing disabled) verified, error rate dropped to baseline.
- 18:15 UTC: targeted host patch rolled to EU pool to correct coalescing boundary condition.
- 01:50 UTC (09/09): rollout completed; final validation run successful.

We confirmed parity between fallback and primary model variants for the request shapes Lagom provided; no content-level drift was observed in the samples you supplied.

Next steps / postmortem:
- We're preparing a short postmortem covering root cause analysis, detection timelines, and long-term fixes (kernel guardrails + KV-cache backpressure smoothing).
- I'll share the postmortem doc link and the planned customer-facing summary by EOD Sept 9 (UTC).
- We're also scheduling a 30-min technical sync with your platform team early next week to review mitigations and make any config adjustments to minimize recurrence.

Attachments: incident-runbook.pdf (internal), statuspage-event-log.txt

Again — sorry for the disruption. If anything else pops up in your logs, please paste the request ids and we'll re-open the investigation immediately.

Thanks for your patience,
Mina Haddad
Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
